signals.signal: Q1-2026 ASF report: at 31/03/2026 the bank ran 2,025 ATMs of which 696 are multifunctional machines (deposit-capable), plus 632 BT Express terminals used for operations other than cash dispensing, over 188,000 installed POS, 47,000 STAR partner locations, 8,400+ e-commerce merchants and 8.2 million cards.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Raport ASF trimestrul I 2026
signals.implies: Supersedes the baseline (~1,800 ATMs / 550+ MFM / 470+ BT Express / 177,000 POS). Romania's largest self-service and acquiring estate, still growing on POS and BT Express. Direct addressable market for Printec ATM/self-service supply, cash recyclers, ATM managed services and POS estate services/terminal supply.
signals.followup: Identify the OEM(s) behind the 2,025 ATMs / 696 MFM / 632 BT Express and who does field service; pull the 30/06/2026 numbers from the H1 ASF report due 21/08/2026.

signals.signal: 2025 annual report gives the full-year series: units in network 531 (2024: 513), ATMs 2,031 (1,937, +4.85%), multifunctional machines 696 (651, +6.91%), BT Express 577, installed POS 178,414 (148,000, +20.55%), STAR partner locations 40,000, cards 8,145,668 (7,172,201), unique digital-channel users 4,928,070 (4,435,953).
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Raport anual 2025 (via BVB infocont)
signals.implies: BT is one of the few CEE banks GROWING its ATM fleet (+94 units in 2025) and adding deposit-capable machines (+45 MFM), against the regional shrink-and-outsource trend. POS grew +30,414 in a single year. Both are live hardware, software and managed-service opportunities for Printec (ATM/recycler supply, cash-management software, POS terminal supply and estate management).
signals.followup: Ask whether the +94 ATMs in 2025 were new purchases or units inherited from OTP Bank Romania; establish the replacement cycle for the ~1,335 cash-out-only units.

signals.signal: AGM of 28/04/2026 approved a 2026 investment programme of RON 1,017.40m incl. VAT (+20.6% vs the 2025 budget) with a line-by-line split: buildings/branches 105.94; IT & cards 663.17 (IT hardware 34.23, IT software 407.82, retail & cards 221.11 of which retail-card hardware 51.92 and retail-card software 169.19); MACHINES 21.39; SECURITY 9.79; CASH-PROCESSING CENTRE 7.88; digital initiatives 177.22; other 32.00. Budget built on a 5.17 RON/EUR planning rate and 6.1% average inflation.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Comunicat privind bugetul pentru anul 2026 (current report) and Raport anual 2025
signals.implies: First time the machine line is isolated: only RON 21.39m (c. EUR 4.1m) of hardware capex for machines against RON 407.82m for IT software. BT buys comparatively little iron and a lot of software - so the highest-value Printec angles are ATM application/monitoring software, cash-management and forecasting software, and managed services, rather than box-shifting. Secondary hard-hardware targets: retail/card hardware RON 51.92m (c. EUR 10m, POS terminals), security RON 9.79m, and the RON 7.88m cash-processing centre (cash automation / sorting).
signals.followup: Confirm with BT procurement what the RON 21.39m machines, RON 9.79m security and RON 7.88m cash-processing-centre lines are committed to, and whether the cash-processing centre is a new build or an upgrade.

signals.signal: Competition Council decision announced 05-07/06/2026: BT is fined RON 875.74m in its own name plus RON 85.03m for the conduct of OTP Bank Romania S.A. (inherited through the 2025 merger) in the ROBOR fixing cartel; total RON 960.77m. BT says it had not yet received the written decision, considers it unfounded and will appeal to the Bucharest Court of Appeal. The Competition Council sanctioned 10 banks for RON 3.73bn in total, its largest fine ever.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Raport curent Decizie Consiliul Concurentei (08/06/2026); Consiliul Concurentei press release
signals.implies: A RON 960.77m hit equal to ~94% of the entire 2026 investment budget, and it is a direct tail liability from the OTP Romania merger. Near-term risk that discretionary hardware capex (the machines / security / cash-centre lines) is deferred while the appeal runs; conversely it strengthens the case for opex-based, no-capex commercial models - ATM-as-a-service, managed services, fixed-fee fleet outsourcing - which is exactly how Printec/ASEE-type deals are structured elsewhere in the region.
signals.likelihood: High that the fine is contested for years; Medium that 2026 hardware capex slips
signals.followup: Watch the H1-2026 results (21/08/2026) for whether BT books a provision for the fine, and the Bucharest Court of Appeal docket; pitch opex/as-a-service self-service models into this constraint.

signals.signal: BT will hold an Investor Day on Thursday 01/10/2026, 10:00-16:00 (c. five hours), covering growth trajectory, business strategy and objectives; registration closes 18/09/2026. It is explicitly separate from the H1-2026 results videoconference on 24/08/2026 (H1 figures published 21/08/2026). Q3 results 20/11/2026, call 23/11/2026.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Invitatie BT Investor Day 2026 (current report) and 2026 financial calendar
signals.implies: BT's first Investor Day of this cycle is the most likely venue for a multi-year technology/capex plan and a channel/distribution strategy (branch vs self-service mix). This is the calendar anchor for positioning a Printec proposal before the 2027 budget is drafted (BT approves budgets at the April AGM).
signals.followup: Register for the 01/10/2026 webcast and mine it for ATM/branch/cash strategy and any multi-year IT envelope; also read the 21/08/2026 H1 ASF report for the 30/06/2026 fleet counts.

signals.signal: Q1-2026: 522 branches/agencies/points of sale at 31/03/2026 vs 532 a year earlier; bank headcount 10,133 (10,180 at 31/12/2025; 10,321 a year earlier), group headcount 13,306; 5 million unique digitalised customers; mobile/NFC merchant payments +24% y/y; card purchases +16% y/y; non-card digital transaction volumes +28% y/y; BT Pay card-to-card transfers +62% y/y; Chat BT past 2 million interactions with 81% self-resolution. Net profit RON 1.14bn (+30.1% y/y), assets RON 227bn.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Rezultate financiare T1 2026 (presentation) and Raport ASF T1 2026
signals.implies: Branch count and headcount are drifting down while the self-service fleet and POS estate grow - the classic push of cash and routine transactions out of the branch. Supports in-branch teller cash recyclers/TCRs, off-site ATM deployment and managed services; the 5m digital customer base and the payment growth rates raise the volume case for digital onboarding/eKYC and transaction-monitoring/AML platforms.
signals.followup: Track branch count per quarter and check whether closures are matched with self-service replacement points; quantify how many of the 522 units still have manual teller cash handling.

signals.signal: On 02/07/2026 BT announced it had completed, with Visa, the first payment in Europe initiated by an AI agent on behalf of a customer using real card data and a merchant's existing infrastructure - executed at Brick Depot LEGO Certified Store, a BT partner merchant, over the Visa Intelligent Commerce platform within the Visa Agentic Ready programme, relying on tokenisation, identity verification and real-time fraud monitoring.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania press release (newsroom); corroborated by Bursa.ro and Startupcafe
signals.implies: BT is pushing its acquiring/issuing stack toward agentic commerce, which raises the bar on tokenisation, identity verification and real-time fraud/transaction monitoring at the merchant edge. Opens a conversation on Printec transaction monitoring, HSM/security and POS/e-commerce acceptance upgrades across the 188,000-terminal estate.
signals.likelihood: Medium - pilot stage, but strategically signposted
signals.followup: Establish who supplies BT's tokenisation/HSM and fraud-monitoring layer today, and whether the agentic pilot triggers a POS/e-commerce acceptance refresh.

signals.signal: 2025 annual report confirms the BT - OTP Bank Romania merger (together with BT Building S.R.L.) was completed on 28/02/2025 and integrated in a record seven months, bringing over 130,000 migrated customers; a simultaneous Victoriabank - BCR Chisinau merger closed 01/03/2025, and BRD Pensii and Microinvest were acquired in the same year. BT's approved 2026 qualitative objectives explicitly keep it open to further acquisitions or mergers that can accelerate expansion.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Raport anual 2025 and Comunicat buget 2026
signals.implies: Integration is finished, so the OTP-inherited estate (ATMs, POS, branches) is now fully inside BT's own fleet numbers - and the remaining M&A appetite means further fleet-harmonisation events are likely. Printec's regional pattern (AikBank/Eurobank Direktna, UniCredit/Alpha RO) is that post-merger dual-fleet harmonisation is the single best entry point for self-service replacement contracts.
signals.likelihood: Medium - further M&A stated as an objective, no target named
signals.followup: Monitor BVB current reports for a new BT acquisition; identify which OEM the ex-OTP Romania ATMs are and whether they are being harmonised or retired.

signals.signal: 2025 annual report: Victoriabank had 67 units (2024: 63), 269 ATMs (252, +6.74%), 10,574 POS (9,064, +16.65%), 635,089 cards (527,501), 6,061 network merchants (5,082) and 363,354 unique digital-channel users at 31/12/2025; assets MDL 31.48bn (+27.84%). Net profit +31% y/y in Q1-2026 and first place in Moldova for instant B2B payments.
signals.source_name: Banca Transilvania - Raport anual 2025 (sustainability statement, BT Group entities)
signals.implies: A small but fast-growing BT-controlled fleet outside the 17-country core view: +17 ATMs and +1,510 POS in one year with a post-merger (BCR Chisinau) estate to harmonise. Addressable for Printec ATM supply/service and POS terminals via the BT Group relationship rather than a standalone Moldova entry.
signals.followup: Check whether BT procurement for Victoriabank is centralised in Cluj or run locally, and identify the incumbent ATM vendor in Moldova.

signals.signal: BNR payment-instrument statistics for 31/12/2025 (released 17/05/2026): 11,136 ATMs supplied by resident PSPs (+1,108 vs June 2025), 729,408 POS terminals (+161,396), 685,731 EFTPOS points (+120,300), and 28.63m active cards of which 24.68m with a cash function.
signals.source_name: AGERPRES reporting Banca Nationala a Romaniei payment statistics
signals.implies: Against the national total, BT's 2,031 ATMs are c.18% of the country's fleet and its 178,414 POS c.24% of terminals - BT alone is roughly a fifth of the Romanian self-service market and a quarter of acceptance. Romania is also still ADDING ATMs, unlike Greece/Cyprus, so it is a growth rather than a rationalisation market for Printec self-service.
signals.followup: Re-source these figures from the BNR interactive database or the Instrumente de plata page directly - bnr.ro blocked automated access this run.

coverage_notes: Fresh run - no checkpoint existed for 2026-07-30, so a full pass was done. Angles used: (1) BT investor-relations primary documents (Q1-2026 results deck 26/05/2026, Q1-2026 ASF quarterly report, 2025 annual report via BVB infocont, 2026 budget current report, financial calendar and calendar amendment, Investor Day invitation); (2) BVB/ASF current-report register for 2026 (all 31 filings listed and the material ones opened - Competition Council decision and investigation status, Investor Day, calendar change); (3) Romanian-language press and search for self-banking, ATM, POS and cash-processing-centre angles; (4) BNR payment statistics for market context; (5) BT newsroom press releases June-July 2026. NEW vs baseline: the whole fleet series is superseded (2,031 ATMs / 696 MFM / 577 BT Express / 178,414 POS at 31/12/2025 and 2,025 / 696 / 632 / >188,000 at 31/03/2026, vs baseline ~1,800 / 550+ / 470+ / 177,000); the 2026 capex table is now broken out line by line including a RON 21.39m machines line and RON 9.79m security line the baseline did not have; the ROBOR fine of RON 875.74m + RON 85.03m for OTP Bank Romania's conduct is entirely new; Investor Day 01/10/2026 and the H1 date of 21/08/2026 are new; the Visa agentic-AI payment of 02/07/2026 is new. RE-VERIFIED: 2026 investment budget RON 1,017.40m incl. VAT +20.6% and the IT/cards 663.17, digital 177.22, buildings 105.94, cash-processing centre 7.88 sub-lines all confirmed against two primary sources; OTP Romania merger completion 28/02/2025 confirmed in the 2025 annual report. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the ATM/MFM/BT Express OEM and the field-service provider are still unnamed anywhere in BT's public filings - BT names only generic categories of suppliers of IT systems and equipment - so the incumbent remains unidentified and is a standing task; (b) BT is a private company, so there is no SEAP/e-licitatie tender trail to mine; (c) H1-2026 numbers are not yet published (due 21/08/2026), so the newest fleet data available is 31/03/2026; (d) the baseline's ~300 Code Crafters IT staff insourced 01/04/2026 could not be re-verified from a primary BT document this run - Code Crafters by BT S.R.L. appears in the 2025 annual report as a group entity but the headcount/date was not restated; (e) the RON 1,017.40m 2025 comparative budget (implied c. RON 843.6m) was not opened directly.
access_issues: www.bancatransilvania.ro returns an HTTP 403 bot-block HTML page to the fetch tool AND to curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent plus Referer/Accept-Language headers. WORKAROUND USED: the identical files are served HTTP 200 from the language subdomains it. / en. / hu.bancatransilvania.ro on the same /files/app/media/... paths - every BT PDF in this part was retrieved that way and text-extracted locally with pdfminer. The 2025 annual report (20.7 MB) was taken from the BVB mirror bvb.ro/infocont/infocont26/. bnr.ro blocked automated access: StatisticsReportHTML.aspx returned a 302 to nothing and Indicatori-plati-5291-Mobile.aspx returned a page with no data rows under a desktop User-Agent, so the BNR ATM/POS totals are cited from AGERPRES (press tier, Low confidence) rather than the regulator directly. consiliulconcurentei.ro returned HTTP 503 on its ROBOR press release, so the fine detail is cited from BT's own current report (primary) with the sector total from search-result summaries only. The BT newsroom press-release detail page for the Visa agentic payment 404'd on the it. subdomain; the canonical www URL is cited and the content corroborated by Bursa.ro and Startupcafe.
